title: Capacitor project setup around an existing web build
when: The user wants to turn a working web app into an installable store app with Capacitor and needs the config, the scripts and an honest view of the native tooling.
inputs: web build command and output folder
prompt:
Goal: The web build wrapped by Capacitor with a correct capacitor.config.json, repeatable sync scripts and a README that states the native tooling needs.
Steps:
1. Add @capacitor/core and @capacitor/cli, then run npx cap init "Field Notes" com.acme.fieldnotes --web-dir dist.
2. capacitor.config.json: { "appId": "com.acme.fieldnotes", "appName": "Field Notes", "webDir": "dist" }; appId never changes after release.
3. webDir is the folder holding the built index.html, not src; build first, then npx cap sync.
4. Add each target with npx cap add plus the platform name; this creates native project folders that you commit.
5. Be honest: compiling needs each platform SDK and its vendor IDE installed (a JDK for one target, a mac with the vendor IDE for the other); npx cap open hands off to that IDE.
6. server.url (live reload from the LAN dev server) stays out of the committed config.
7. package.json scripts: "build" and "cap:sync" that runs the build then npx cap sync.
Quality bar:
- A fresh clone builds with two commands.
Pitfalls:
- Shipping server.url, so the store app loads from a laptop.
- Absolute asset paths that break inside the WebView.
Verify:
- [ ] capacitor.config.json has appId, appName and webDir.
- [ ] The webDir folder contains index.html after the build.
- [ ] No server.url in the committed config.
- [ ] README lists the SDKs and IDEs needed.
Output: capacitor.config.json, package.json scripts and a README build section.

examples.input: transforma meu app web em app de loja com Capacitor
examples.output: capacitor.config.json (appId, appName, webDir dist), cap:sync script, README naming the SDKs and IDEs
